A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Turbo Connection research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, accuracy and training-time measurements, ablations, parity length generalization, discriminative filtering and CoT experiments in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluation of NuminaMath-trained checkpoints on AMC/AIME competition problems in Section 4.8.1 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The cross-token residual connections, projections, initialization, grouping mechanism and training objective remain unchanged, as do the listed model-specific connections. V2's Algorithm 1 and wiring-selection explanation document the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: V2 adds transfer evaluation on pooled 2023 AMC and 2024–2025 AIME problems. This extends the existing mathematical-reasoning coverage to a competition-test population using NuminaMath-trained checkpoints; the earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: The standard Transformer and single soft-token comparators remain in their corresponding experiments. The new competition evaluation extends the existing baseline-plus-CoT comparison. Universal Transformers, feedback memory and Staircase Attention receive discussion but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.8.1 adds a transfer-testing protocol using NuminaMath-trained checkpoints and the existing CoT-generation procedure with identical inference hyperparameters. Earlier splits, training budgets, model configurations and temperatures remain unchanged. The newly specified GSM8K filtering threshold clarifies an already reported preprocessing step.

E4.justification: The new competition-math experiment tests whether CoT-correction benefits transfer beyond the training dataset. Existing group-size and multiplier analyses, soft-token comparison, parity length-generalization experiment and discriminative-filtering analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. V2's statement about zero or one wiring-selection trials concerns hyperparameter selection, not repeated measurements or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds AMC/AIME transfer accuracies of 2.00% for Baseline + CoT and 4.45% for TurboConn + CoT. Previously reported accuracies, training times, filtering measurements and Figure 4 curves are unchanged after matching v1 Tables 1/2 to v2 Tables 2/1.

T1.justification: V2 formalizes the wiring heuristic as a connection-set definition in Appendix A.5. Appendix A.6.3 also corrects the Qwen parameter-count substitution from 17,772,768 to 10,367,448, making it consistent with the retained total of 141,111,768. The central computational-depth arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about depth scaling, reasoning improvements, dense feedback, parity performance and generation efficiency. The added transfer experiment supports the existing contribution without redefining the paper's core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges sequential prefill as an inference-latency bottleneck and expands the efficiency comparison with Universal Transformers. It also interprets competition results as correction of imperfect CoTs and argues for wiring robustness from minimal configuration search; these are new qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds forward-pass pseudocode specifying caching, injection and extraction, plus an explanation of wiring selection. Section 4.4 specifies the existing GSM8K filter: over 168 Llama-tokenizer tokens, removing 44 of 384,620 examples. These supplement the already detailed connection lists, hyperparameters and CoT-training instructions.

R1.justification: V2 adds Fan et al. (2021) on feedback memory and Ju et al. (2022) on Staircase Attention, positioning TurboConn around augmentation of pretrained LLMs through zero-initialized additive connections. It expands the Universal Transformer comparison and adds sources for the competition datasets.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. V2 makes localized grammar corrections, corrects the author name from Sidu to Sidi, adds explanatory subsections and an acknowledgment, and renumbers appendix sections after inserting the pseudocode section.

P2.justification: V2 removes the conceptual engine illustration, moves v1's architecture Figure 2 to Figure 1, renumbers the grouping diagram and adds a dense-connectivity Figure 3. It also adds an algorithm display, expands Table 5 and relocates tables, including exchanging the numbering of the main-results and efficiency tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through pseudocode, preprocessing and wiring-selection details, explicit acknowledgment of prefill costs, and closer positioning against earlier feedback architectures. It also fixes an inconsistent parameter-count calculation and adds limited transfer evidence. The new competition results lack a stated test-set size and uncertainty estimates, while wiring robustness is inferred from minimal search, so the overall improvement remains modest.
